title: De Amore (The Art of Courtly Love)
shelf_note: Andreas Capellanus, De Amore — belongs in arlima (medieval literature); a canonical medieval Latin text.
structure_note: 213 pages, 213 OCR, 209 translated; printed page numbers track the image index (scan 53 = p.35, 105 = p.87, 157 = p.139), so the run is consistent. Nothing stands out.

tr_errors.source: [71] Nuntius sum quidem vobis ab amoris aula trans-
tr_errors.english: I am indeed a messenger sent to you from the court of love, who commands your prudence to untie the knot of a certain doubt: namely, whose probity is more to be praised, that of the woman noble by blood, or of her who is known to be destitute of the nobility of lineage?
tr_errors.problem: the translation runs on past the page's last word and includes a sentence from the next leaf (lookahead)

tr_errors.source: Regulariter enim tibi trado, Gualteri
tr_errors.english: For I teach you regularly, Gualterius
tr_errors.problem: 'regulariter' means 'as a rule', not 'regularly'

tr_errors.source: quod tam prudenter omnibus pro meritis respondere voluistis
tr_errors.english: because you wished to respond so prudently to all my merits
tr_errors.problem: the Latin means 'to answer everyone according to their merits'; the translation narrows it to 'my merits'

tr_errors.source: tituunt merita potiorem, etsi alter a vobis spem largitam suscepisset amoris.
tr_errors.english: (omitted)
tr_errors.problem: the page's opening clause, which ends the sentence carried over from the previous leaf, is not translated

tr_errors.source: suis nitimini probitatem iniuste meritis defraudare
tr_errors.english: you strive to defraud integrity of its unjustly earned merits
tr_errors.problem: 'iniuste' qualifies the defrauding ('you unjustly try to cheat worth of its merits'), not the merits; the translation says the merits were unjustly earned

tr_errors.source: qui sua coram
tr_errors.english: who would not hesitate to propose his rights or request the gifts of love in your presence. That, however, you said that the betterness of another ought not to generate prejudice ... the petition of a worthier person who comes later.
tr_errors.problem: two sentences from the next leaf are added after the page's last word (lookahead)

other.note: the editor's bracketed passage '[nisi forte amoris ... denegare petenti]' is wrapped in a <note>…</note> tag in the translation, so a reader sees the editor's bracketed text as a translator's note
running head 'DE AMORE 87' is translated as the first line of the reader text

ocr_errors.ocr: **Capitulum VII. — De variis iudiciis amoris**
ocr_errors.image: [271] Capitulum VII. — De variis iudiciis amoris
ocr_errors.problem: editor's section numbers [271] and [272] (inside 'ef[272]ficiar') dropped

other.note: a raw '<header>DE AMORE 139</header>' tag is the first line of the translation

book_verdict: Clean OCR of a 1929 edition, and the translations are faithful in substance. But two of three pages carry sentences from the next leaf, a leaked <header> tag, and the editor's brackets turned into a <note>. Readable, but the seams show.

title: Contra Celsum (1481 editio princeps)
shelf_note: Origen against Celsus in Persona's Latin, Rome 1481 incunable; it belongs with late-antique pagan/Christian polemic and is adjacent to the Hermetica.
structure_note: 538 pages, all OCR'd, 524 translated; no printed foliation is visible on these leaves. Nothing stands out.

ocr_errors.image: uti Celſus exiſtimat
ocr_errors.problem: small slip

tr_errors.english: except to those suffering from madness, frenzy, or madness
tr_errors.problem: doubled 'madness'

other.note: the translation opens with a '<meta>Continuity: Continues the defense of the resurrection…</meta>' line shown as reader text

tr_errors.source: …demonſtrabimus: quis autem qui moderatior ſit … ut condita fuerint hec omnia demõſtrare.
tr_errors.english: "But so that I may not speak only of the Jews … we will demonstrate more openly what was said above. For who, being more moderate … not more for the sake of men than for brute animals."
tr_errors.problem: the closing quotation mark is misplaced, so Origen's own rebuttal ('who … would not suppress the impudence of this man…') is printed as Celsus's words

tr_errors.source: in quibus ſibi amãtiſſimi quidam collaudant̃
tr_errors.english: in which they themselves are highly praised by their most loving friends
tr_errors.problem: inverted: it is their dearest friends who are praised for the same things

ocr_errors.image: quādoqdē parētes (quandoquidem)
ocr_errors.problem: 'quandoquidem' (since) split; the translation then reads it as 'sometimes … when'

tr_errors.source: quādoq̄ d̄e parētes ipſi & filiis ī ſe decertātibus ſiue cōfecti iã ſenio nulli uſui ſint: ſiue delirēt
tr_errors.english: which quails sometimes enter into between themselves, when the parents themselves and the sons are struggling against each other, or if they are already worn out by old age
tr_errors.problem: the sense is 'since the parents, while their sons fight, are either worn out by age … or senile'; the clause is muddled

book_verdict: Good abbreviation-resolving OCR of a hard incunable type, and translations that are mostly faithful. One misplaced quotation boundary puts Origen's words in Celsus's mouth, and a <meta> continuity line leaks on p.135.

title: Catalogus ingenuorum iuvenum … in Collegio D. Nicolai … in Bruck …
shelf_note: A manuscript register of student pledges to Bishop Johannes Fabri's Vienna college (St Nicholas), 1536–1540: an institutional/university-history document with no collection or tradition attached, outside the library's esoteric and early-science core.
structure_note: All three sampled images are two-page openings that were never split; the OCR labels each as '<columns>2</columns>' with a <column-break/>, so each 'page' is really two leaves (I3). 36 pages / 35 translated. The entries are dated 1536 (p.11) and 1540 (p.28), consistent with a register kept over years.

title: Boethius De consolatione philosophiae
shelf_note: 13th-century glossed manuscript of Boethius; core medieval philosophy (no collection assigned).
structure_note: 158 pages, 150 OCR, 136 translated: 8 leaves have no OCR and 14 OCR'd leaves are untranslated, so coverage is uneven. The foliation (35 on image 81) fits a codex with front matter.
